tldr: Three arXiv papers from Oct 14–22 apply on-policy distillation (training a student on its own sampled trajectories, scored by a teacher) to different problems: machine translation, long-horizon coding agents, and the question of when the teacher should lead.
whats_new: Oct 22: an arXiv paper proposes advantage-based on-policy distillation, deciding per step when the student should follow the teacher.
why_it_matters: On-policy distillation is spreading from general post-training into narrow jobs (translation, coding agents), so teams distilling small models should compare it against SFT on their own trajectories.

beats.headline: Qwen-MT-Lumen applies on-policy training to WMT 2026 translation
OPRD distills constraint reminders into long-horizon coding agents
Advantage-based method decides when to follow the teacher

open_questions: Does the advantage-based method beat plain on-policy distillation on agentic coding tasks, not only its own benchmarks?
Does any group release code that reproduces the OPRD long-horizon results?
take_for_builders: If you distill small models, run an on-policy versus SFT comparison on your own task trajectories before adopting either method; none of these papers has independent replication yet.
